objects.original: Euclidean objective, its gradient, fixed-step GD and objective gap.
objects.reconstructed: Actual Riesz gradient and N-fold iteration of x ↦ x-h∇f(x).
objects.evidence: The printed Lean statement, entire supplied module and blind reconstruction agree; no arbitrary vector field or assumed sequence replaces actual gradient descent.

domains.original: Euclidean space; iteration count; source denominators impose unstated restrictions.
domains.reconstructed: Complete real inner-product space; real parameters; h>0 and natural N>0. Also α>0, 0≤q=1-αh<1; inverse-power branch requires q>0.
domains.evidence: Space is generalized. Positive h and N are substantive explicit domain restrictions, not a literal match to printed h≤1/β. βh≤1 agrees with that upper restriction when β>0. Lean omits β≥0, and also handles β=0 without division by β.

quantifiers.original: Displayed rate compares to a minimizer; equation (3.3) permits every comparator.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every x₀,z and positive N; global upper model for every x,y.
quantifiers.evidence: Arbitrary z is a disclosed extension of the displayed final rate supported by the general-comparator energy argument. Monotonicity of f(X_n), nonnegative weights, and nonnegativity of squared distance suffice even when f(X_N)-f(z)<0. No minimizer existence or optimality assumption is hidden.

assumptions.original: Section 3: C²; convexity and Definition 1.12 smoothness.
assumptions.reconstructed: C1; α-strong convexity with α/2 normalization, α>0, αh≤1; global quadratic upper model, h>0 and βh≤1.
assumptions.evidence: The quadratic upper model is the source definition (1.7), not an extra replacement for a source Lipschitz hypothesis. C1 weakens the section C² convention. Explicit positive-step and positive-iteration hypotheses exclude genuine singular or invalid cases. The added αh≤1 ensures nonnegative recurrence weights; in a nontrivial Euclidean source setting α≤β gives it from the step restriction.

conclusion.original: Theorem 3.4 has one-step energy and normalized value bounds, with convex specialization.
conclusion.reconstructed: Strong rational bound and conditional inverse-power bound.
conclusion.evidence: The binding supports only inverse-power-rate. For 0<q<1, αq^N R²/[2(1-q^N)]=αR²/[2(q^(-N)-1)]. The internal heq proof establishes this equality, although it is not a separately exported equality theorem. At q=0 only the rational bound applies.

scopes.original: Full cited item includes energy, weighted proof, positive-curvature rate and convex interpretation.
scopes.reconstructed: One named public normalized-rate component, using an existing weighted parent.
scopes.evidence: This declaration does not independently establish every source obligation. The supplied whole module contains both normalized-rate interfaces and imports the existing energy/weighted module. No new distance contraction, minimizer existence, iteration-complexity theorem, or continuous-parameter limit follows from this binding alone. The lesson and binding retain this scope.

constant_dependencies.original: Coefficients depend on curvature, step, iteration count and initial distance.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: αq^N R²/[2(1-q^N)] and αR²/[2(q^(-N)-1)] on their specified domains.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The 1/2 normalization is preserved. β affects admissibility rather than the general-step coefficient; there is no dimension constant. N>0 and 0≤q<1 ensure 1-q^N>0; strict q>0 ensures inverse cancellation and a positive inverse-power denominator.

deltas.description: Positive h and N repair a source domain omission.
deltas.evidence: For f(t)=t²/2, x₀=1, z=0, β=1, h=-1 and N=1, the convex bound would assert 2≤-1/2. The printed upper-step inequality alone permits this. h=0 or N=0 also makes the ordinary normalized denominator singular. The candidate explicitly excludes all these cases.

deltas.description: Disclosed C1 Hilbert-space and comparator generalizations preserve the supported source specialization.
deltas.evidence: The candidate assumptions and blind reconstruction expose the wider space, weaker regularity, and unrestricted comparator. Euclidean C² instances and z=x⋆ recover the source setting on admissible coefficient domains.

deltas.description: This is public-interface integration of an existing weighted theorem, not evidence that all source obligations or all proof algebra are new.
deltas.evidence: The module visibly calls GradientDescentValue.gradient_descent_weighted_value_bound. Its documentation and lesson explicitly attribute prior normalization algebra to test consumers. Those external test files and build evidence were outside this review packet, so their existence, historical priority and compilation are not independently certified here.

deltas.description: The printed inverse-power expression needs a positive-base restriction or an explicit limiting endpoint convention.
deltas.evidence: At α=β=h=1, N=1, f(t)=t²/2, x₀=1 and z=0, q=0 and the true gap is 0. Ordinary q^(-N) is undefined; Lean totalized inverse would give a right side of -1/2. The conditional branch correctly avoids that false reading, and the rational branch gives 0. This is not literal full-domain equivalence to (3.2).

review_evidence: Accepted as an accurately described, narrowly bound publication component, not as exact full-source equivalence or approval of any repair overlay. Independent read: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3, especially the section assumptions, Theorem 3.4, (3.3), Lemma 3.5 and its following weighted calculation; Definition 1.12 fixes smoothness. Compared these against the supplied entire module, declaration, lesson, binding and source-blind reconstruction. The component mathematics and formula proof agree. The strong proof retains 0≤q<1 for its rational rate, proves inverse conversion only for 0<q<1, and does not claim the singular inverse-power endpoint. Needed source repair, recorded for separate review only: require h>0 and N>0 for normalized rates; require β>0 whenever writing h=1/β. For the inverse-power formula require α>0 and αh<1; state the rational formula separately at αh=1 and the convex formula separately at α=0. No repair is proposed or approved in repairs here. The full source item remains broader than this supported obligation. Source-independent build verification must still check the imported parent, genuine compiled consumer tests, historical integration claims and repository gate; packet compiled=true is not independent build evidence. No registry, route reports, previous verdicts or repair proposals were read.
